statuses.guaranteed: Deterministic and blocking. Implemented, and a behavioural test proves it.
statuses.advisory: Projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours it is not observable from outside. Documentation, not enforcement.
statuses.planned: Specified and not implemented. Named so the omission is visible.
statuses.rejected: Considered and deliberately refused, with the reason recorded.

edge_kinds.specified_by: the document that defines the claim
edge_kinds.proved_by: the behavioural test that proves it

nodes.label: The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key
nodes.note: A restricted YAML subset. Tabs, anchors, flow maps and multi-line scalars are refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.label: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist
Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
nodes.note: The path must exist, be executable, and be invoked by the named dispatcher. A hook that invokes it and discards the exit code counts as not wired.

nodes.label: Exit codes are a contract, and no code means "warn and continue"
Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
nodes.note: Running update twice leaves the byte-identical file. The test asserts the hash.

nodes.label: Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected
A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
nodes.note: How a repository that already has a hand-written CLAUDE.md adopts Majordomus. An edit outside the markers is never drift; an edit inside them is caught. Malformed markers are refused, not guessed at.

nodes.label: Wiring is found in a hook or in any subhook of the directory that hook dispatches to
nodes.note: The finding names the file that actually carries the invocation. A subhook that is not executable is reported as not wired, because the dispatcher skips it.

nodes.label: Every rule the tool enforces is declared once, as a rule object in the repository's effective set, and doctor proves each one is reached by the command that claims to run it
nodes.note: A doctrine whose validator does not exist, a validator no doctrine declares, a command that never dispatches, a blocking rule whose command cannot exit non-zero, a missing test, and CI that swallows the suite are six separate failures with six separate messages. Each is mutation-tested.

nodes.label: A doctrine's class is what decides whether a violation stops the command, not a label beside it
nodes.note: The test changes checkpoint freshness from advisory to blocking in a copy of the vendored rule file and asserts that check's exit code moves from 0 to 10. There are two classes and no override.

nodes.label: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event, and a malformed line is a failure rather than a skipped record
nodes.note: The reader skips a bad line rather than crashing, and check, doctor and watch all report it. The ledger is the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct.

nodes.label: A decision record without a task, a head and a reason is reported, and does not block
nodes.note: decisions.md is hand-editable by design, so an unattributable entry is a warning. finish still refuses when a profile requires a record it cannot find.

nodes.label: An entry in the questions store that does not parse blocks acceptance exactly as an unresolved question does
nodes.note: A gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one, so an unreadable question is not a lesser problem than an open one.

nodes.label: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure
nodes.note: Covers name and filename mismatch, an empty description, an unknown front-matter key, missing front matter, and a block token used inline.

nodes.label: A use case or application cannot name a command, doctrine or claim that does not exist, and the two catalogues cannot disagree about which applies to which
nodes.note: Prose describing the tool is checked the same way the tool checks itself. Cross-references are verified in both directions, so a use case naming an application that does not name it back is a failure rather than a silent asymmetry. An application declaring no does_not_fit_when is refused, because a catalogue that only lists fits is marketing.

nodes.label: A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
nodes.note: update refuses, offers a diff, and overwrites only under an explicit flag.

nodes.label: The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check
nodes.note: Over budget, nothing is written at all.

nodes.label: Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve
A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
Installing into a repository that already has an installation is refused
Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
Nothing performs a network call, evaluates generated text, or deletes recursively
A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
nodes.note: A scope path that escapes the repository root is refused. Starting a second task while one is active is refused.

nodes.label: Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored
nodes.note: A handover body that tries to set one is rejected rather than merged.

nodes.label: check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now
A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
State read back is labelled exact, advanced, diverged or different_context against git
Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
nodes.note: Reported, never blocking. Work in progress is reported and never blocked.

nodes.label: watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift
handover writes an append-only record with computed front matter and required sections
nodes.note: A body with a missing or empty required section is refused and names the sections.

nodes.label: Handovers carry durable facts, never conversation transcripts
finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet
An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
nodes.note: no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist. failed means the work could not be done. They are different facts.

nodes.label: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
nodes.note: The axes are validated and projected into the worker's instructions. Whether a worker honours them is not observable from outside the worker.

nodes.label: A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model
nodes.note: Mapping a class to a concrete model is left to whoever runs the worker. Majordomus never selects or invokes a model.

nodes.label: A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more
nodes.note: majordomus context now assembles a briefing from those toggles, and that selection is guaranteed (see context-assembly). This claim stays advisory because nothing measures what the worker actually read once it has been handed the briefing.

nodes.label: Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed
A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported
nodes.note: The staleness report is guaranteed. Whether the worker checkpoints is not.

nodes.label: The context a worker is given is assembled from durable state in authority order, and what a profile excludes is excluded
nodes.note: Git first, then task and profile, then blockers, then authored records, then history. The profile's context block decides what is offered; it is the only code that reads those fields.

nodes.label: The assembled context obeys a line budget, and every section it drops is named with its reason
nodes.note: The count is of the printed document, not of its sections. Git, task, profile and open blockers are never dropped; record bodies degrade to a pointer before they disappear.

nodes.label: A checkpoint is a capped progress record with computed identity, and a body over the cap is refused rather than truncated
nodes.note: The cap is what keeps a checkpoint distinct from a handover. Mode 0600, created atomically, never staged.

nodes.label: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
nodes.note: Same worktree and branch, else same branch, else nothing. Ties within one second are broken by ledger order. Absence is reported as absence.

nodes.label: The ledger is readable back as operational history, filtered by task, event and time
nodes.note: What happened, when, for which task, at which head, and what outcome was accepted. Never what anyone said.

nodes.label: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
nodes.note: Refuses to overwrite an existing archive, and does nothing when the ledger is under its cap.

nodes.label: A decision is recorded with its reason and its task, and is superseded by a later entry rather than edited
nodes.note: --why is required. --supersedes refuses text matching no recorded decision. Task and head are computed.

nodes.label: An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an entry the gate cannot parse is a failure rather than a silent pass
nodes.note: A gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one, so check, doctor and watch all fail on a malformed entry.

nodes.label: A repository-local prompt renders against a closed set of state tokens, and an unknown token is an error
nodes.note: No conditionals, loops, includes or shell. A prompt that silently renders a misspelled token as literal text is worse than one that refuses.

nodes.label: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
nodes.note: A fixed-string grep in authority order. No ranking, no embedding, no index that could fall out of step with the records it describes.

nodes.label: Every continuity store is proven reachable through its own command, not merely present on disk
nodes.note: doctor runs the resolver, renders every prompt asset, validates both parsed stores and builds the context. A directory of records that no command reads is the failure this tool exists to catch.

nodes.label: The context that applies to a path is composed from the layer's scoped documents, root to target, in one deterministic order with provenance, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing
nodes.note: A document is a Markdown file under .ai/ whose front matter carries schema context/v1; the file name is a convention and the id is the identity. Ordering is depth, then declared order, then path. Providers and audience filter; extend, replace and final compose; a duplicate id, a dangling reference, a superseded final document or a cycle is refused by name.

nodes.label: The impact of a change set on the scoped context is reported from git — the documents, the scopes below them, moves with their ancestry, tracked sources to review, and stale projections — and an unrelated change reports nothing
nodes.note: context affected reads the working tree, the index, or a base ref, with renames detected; a tracked source change is a WARN to review and never an exit code, because the tool cannot decide whether prose still describes code. context check-sync is validate, then every projection against its stamp, then affected; test/cases/71_context_sync.sh proves the exit codes.

nodes.label: The repository's AI layer is one directory whose manifest names every section, readable without the tool
nodes.note: init seeds .ai/ from the skeleton and nothing else; no hook, no shell file, no tool installation. doctor fails on a section the manifest names that is absent, and on a manifest key nothing reads.

nodes.label: Checkout-local state lives under .ai/local/, is ignored by git, and is absent on a fresh clone or worktree
nodes.note: The task record, ledger, decisions, questions, checkpoints and handovers never travel through git. A record that arrives in another checkout by other means names the checkout it belongs to and is enforced nowhere else, which test/cases/27_foreign_task.sh proves.

nodes.label: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused
nodes.note: rules vendor status reports an edited, missing or stray file; rules vendor update refuses over it until --force, and never touches rules/project/. A newer executable reports a newer package and does not apply it.

nodes.label: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing
nodes.note: A missing or deprecated dependency, a cycle, one identity claimed twice, a project rule in the vendor namespace, malformed front matter, an unknown key and an x-majordomus block missing its binding are each refused by name. Every dependency is listed before the rule that depends on it, and two runs agree.

nodes.label: Provider instruction files are thin bootstraps that point at the AI layer and carry no rule of their own
nodes.note: Every projection names .ai/README.md, README.md names AGENTS.md, and doctor fails on a projection that grew a rules section of its own. A person and a worker reach the same layer by the same two hops.

nodes.label: A repository on the pre-.ai layout is migrated once, explicitly, with a previewed plan and a verified backup of its local state, and the command is idempotent afterwards
nodes.note: Every other command refuses the legacy layout and names migrate. --dry-run prints the plan and writes nothing. A file the version does not know is reported, never deleted; a destination that already exists refuses the whole run.

nodes.label: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository
nodes.note: A checkout copy, an unrelated absolute path and a PATH install read the same repository files and write nothing into the distribution, whose hash is the same after every command. The distribution root is derived from the entry point, never from the environment.

nodes.label: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range
nodes.note: Today scope is checked with git diff base..HEAD, and a commit range has no author, so another session committing to the same branch in the same checkout has its files counted as this task's work. Recording each commit as it happens turns the question from a heuristic about ranges into an enumeration. The list would be a lookup that git overrules, never authority, and a rewritten commit would be reported as unrecognised rather than resolved to a guess.

nodes.label: What the tool knows about itself is written once and derived everywhere else, and a second copy is a test failure
nodes.note: Policy values have no reader-side defaults, claim statuses are declared in the matrix, the site fixtures derive their inputs from the generator, and every command, doctrine and claim is checked against a list read from the dispatch table or the registry rather than written into the test.

nodes.label: The public command surface is declared, and reconciled against the dispatcher
nodes.note: The registry is authority for what a command means; bin/majordomus stays authority for what runs. A command dispatched with no entry, and an entry nothing dispatches, both fail. A command is public exactly when the usage text lists it, checked in both directions.

nodes.label: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed rather than remembered
nodes.note: The requirement is derived from the registry, so a command added tomorrow is owed coverage from that moment. Coverage is declared in per-case headers rather than inferred, because the negative assertions that use stdin and the surface case's loop are invisible to any scan.

nodes.label: The ledger's event vocabulary is closed, on the way in and on the way out
nodes.note: share/events.yaml declares every name, its emitting command and its required payload keys. An unregistered name is refused on write, refused as a history filter, and reported by history --validate when already stored.

nodes.label: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented
nodes.note: The corpus is a handful of Markdown files and one JSONL. An index or an embedding store would be a second source of truth that has to be kept in step with the first, and a scan is faster than that problem. Revisited only if a repository appears where the scan is measurably too slow.

nodes.label: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope
nodes.note: The record is checkout-local and never tracked, so it does not travel through git; one that arrives by other means is recognised by the worktree it names. check, finish --check and watch report a foreign record and enforce nothing from it; finish refuses to write to it. A record from before the field existed is treated as local, so upgrading does not turn an installation red.

nodes.label: A blocking question keeps blocking after the work is handed to a new task
nodes.note: The gate reads every unresolved entry in the store rather than only the active task's, so a handover cannot launder a blocker. The store is checkout-local, so the questions a gate can see are the ones asked in this working copy. Only a completed finish is refused; blocked, partial, no_match and failed are honest non-completions and are not. Any task may resolve any question. The alternatives — transferring the question with the handover, or gating on scope overlap — were rejected in M001 with the case each gets wrong.

nodes.label: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
nodes.note: The one implementation studied was rolled back within days because its limits were global constants rather than task-derived.

nodes.label: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
nodes.note: Nothing measures token spend today. Any estimated_ field is labelled and excluded from enforcement.

nodes.label: Cost per accepted outcome will be reported from measured data only
Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
nodes.note: Recommendations only. Majordomus does not invoke a model.

nodes.label: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers
A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented
nodes.note: Refused for task records, and only for them. Issues and milestones do carry dependencies, validated as two graphs — see docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/PLANNING.md. What stays refused is a task, the record of one session's work, waiting on another; one task is active per checkout and coordination between checkouts is the scope overlap report. The original wording said no dependency graph existed anywhere, which stopped being true when the plan model landed.

nodes.label: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error
nodes.note: The same allowlist rule the policy and the profiles live under. The filename is the id; a record that disagrees with its own filename is refused rather than reconciled.

nodes.label: Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere
nodes.note: An issue records started_at, verified_at, completed_at, cancelled and its evidence. BLOCKED, READY, ACTIVE, VERIFY, DONE and CANCELLED follow from those and from the state of its dependencies. `status` is not a field, so writing one is an unknown key.

nodes.label: A cycle, a self-dependency and a dependency on an issue that does not exist are each refused by name
nodes.note: Kahn layering; the issues that never leave the graph are the ones reported. A malformed graph fails doctor and is reported by watch as drift.

nodes.label: Execution waves are computed from the graph, and issues in one wave that touch the same paths are reported as serialised
nodes.note: Sharing a wave is necessary for concurrency, not sufficient. Overlapping declared scope serialises conservatively, because a false serialisation costs time and a false parallel costs a conflict.

nodes.label: An issue cannot be completed while a required piece of evidence is missing
nodes.note: Evidence is a command and its result, or an artifact. Narrative is refused. An issue whose completed_at is set but whose evidence is incomplete derives VERIFY, never DONE.

nodes.label: The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it
nodes.note: The sequence is the topological rank of the milestone graph, so no list of versions exists anywhere. While a hand-written roadmap table survives, the doctrine holds it to the model in both directions; once it is gone the check holds trivially, which is the regression it exists to refuse.

nodes.label: GitHub milestones and issues are generated from the canonical model, and a hand-edited generated region is reported rather than overwritten
nodes.note: The adapter lives in scripts/ because the tool itself makes no network call, which test/cases/08_no_forbidden_constructs.sh proves. The begin marker carries the hash of the record it was generated from, which is what separates a moved plan from a hand edit.

nodes.label: The Rust executable serves the repository's AI layer to an MCP client over stdio, read-only, with protocol frames alone on stdout
nodes.note: One process per client, alive as long as its pipe; diagnostics go to stderr; a session leaves the repository byte-identical. The crate's own suite, tests/mcp_stdio.rs, holds the same frames to the same rules.

nodes.label: What the MCP server serves is decided by the manifest, the declared source classes and each file's front matter, so an object added to the layer is served with no change to the executable
nodes.note: The add, remove and break sequence through the built binary is tests/external_extension.rs in the crate; the shell case proves the layer init writes is served, and that a rule added to it appears.

nodes.label: A file of the layer the MCP server cannot read is excluded with a diagnostic naming its path and the index says it is degraded, never silently smaller
nodes.note: Two files of one kind claiming one identity are both excluded and both named. --strict refuses to serve a degraded layer; --inspect exits 10 on one.

nodes.label: Every capability of the Rust executable is defined once, and the registry refuses a duplicate id or a colliding projection name, naming both parties
nodes.note: Two sources, builtin executables and the layer's objects, meet in one registry built at one place; ids, MCP names and URIs, HTTP routes and CLI paths are each unique or the registry does not build. The crate's tests/registry.rs covers every collision.

nodes.label: MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, the capabilities commands and the generated reference are derived from the registry, and a change to one definition reaches every one of them
nodes.note: No projection declares a name, a description, a schema or a route of its own; tests/projections.rs proves every declared projection present and none orphan, and that a changed input type and description reach the MCP schema, the OpenAPI operation and the reference. MCP and HTTP answer the same handler identically.

nodes.label: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change
nodes.note: share/kinds.yaml and share/schemas/*.schema.json are the distribution's; .ai/repo/knowledge/kinds.yaml and schemas/ are the repository's; a name declared by both is an error naming both files. The shell tool's allow-lists are generated from the same schemas.

nodes.label: The committed projections, the OpenAPI document, the capability reference and the allow-lists, are regenerated from the registry and the schemas, and generate --check refuses a stale one
nodes.note: Byte-identical on regeneration, no timestamps, no absolute paths; --check writes nothing and exits 10 naming every file that differs or is missing. CI runs it.

nodes.label: One shared server serves a repository: the first majordomus mcp binds loopback HTTP with Swagger UI and MCP over HTTP beside its stdio session and logs the URL, every later one attaches to it, and it ends when the last client leaves
nodes.note: The election is one lease file under .ai/local/state/mcp/, created atomically and removed on exit; a stale lease is taken over; a bridged client whose server dies takes over or re-attaches without its client noticing. The crate's tests/mcp_shared.rs covers the socket side; --standalone keeps one process per client.

nodes.label: Every client attached to the shared server is a peer named by its own initialize, listed by majordomus_peers, and majordomus_announce tells the others what it is working on and which paths it expects to touch
nodes.note: Two registry capabilities, peers.list (a query) and peers.announce (the one command), projected like every other; the board is one process's memory and is gone with it. Announcements are informational; scope is enforced by the shell tool's task record, not here.

nodes.label: An MCP client opened in the repository starts the server itself, building the executable when it must, through the client configurations at the root and bin/majordomus-mcp
nodes.note: .mcp.json (Claude Code), .gemini/settings.json (Gemini CLI) and .codex/config.toml (Codex) name the same launcher, which writes nothing to stdout and passes every argument to majordomus mcp; MAJORDOMUS_BIN, MAJORDOMUS_BUILD_PROFILE and MAJORDOMUS_NO_BUILD control the build.
